Routines for spare blankets on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and this page teaches why

Spare blankets seem simple, but they matter because they help keep companion animals calm, clean, and comfortable while we handle check-in and transfer steps. At the Companion Animal Travel Desk, we treat each blanket as part of the animal's care plan, not as an extra item to toss aside. If a traveler arrives nervous, a spare blanket can lower stress, reduce sliding in the carrier, and make the handoff feel steadier for both the animal and the owner.

Start by checking that the blanket is clean, dry, and free of loose threads before you offer it. If it smells stale, feels damp, or has fur buildup, set it aside for laundering instead of using it at the desk. Keep the folded stack neat, and never press a blanket into a carrier without first making sure it will not block airflow or crowd the pet. When a traveler needs reassurance, explain the purpose in a calm voice and keep your wording short.

For rabbit travel, follow the file exactly as written and avoid guessing at limits or document dates. <<FACT F064>> A rabbit can seem settled one moment and tense the next, so staff should handle the carrier gently and avoid sudden movements. <<FACT F082>> If the health paperwork looks unclear, pause the handoff and bring in the senior coordinator before continuing.

When you restock, place the clean blankets where they are easy to reach but not in the way of leashes, labels, or routing papers. If a blanket is used during a delay, log it for cleaning right away so the next shift does not have to sort through worn items. This habit keeps the desk orderly and helps every animal get steady, respectful care.

Remember that a spare blanket is a small tool with a big job, so use it carefully and with good judgment.
